issues.description: The package contains no full author input panel. The two SAS programs read distinct EPS, non-EPS/GPS, consensus, guidance, CRSP, Compustat, ExecuComp, insider, index and IR files. Catalog matches are product candidates only; exact prepared schemas, field mapping, vintage, access and complete history remain unverified.

The consumed RAW.DAILY_RET requires NCUSIP for the actual announcement join. Frozen CRSP DSF metadata lists CUSIP but does not provide NCUSIP; the required source-specific crosswalk or author-prepared DAILY_RET mapping is not supplied. Do not assume CUSIP=NCUSIP.

Additional_Input.sas writes SE_190516 to RESULT, but its later PROC DOWNLOAD writes DELTA under the re-bound local RESULT_202008 root; KMX_Code.sas reads RESULT.SE_190516 and RESULT.DELTA. KMX SAS output roots and exported DTA roots also vary. Configure or stage these produced files consistently before KMX.

Several cross-sectional median-split snippets are only in SAS block comments and spell EGEN, XTILE and REPLACE in uppercase. The nested _gxtile helper is found by Stata 18 metadata, but command/function/option token-case compatibility remains unknown; keep the supplied variable-name case and resolve token spelling through primary Stata help before any later authorized run.

KMX_Code.sas creates WORK.DELTA from RESULT.DELTA and adds numeric GVKEY_N, but the next SQL join reads RESULT.DELTA directly and references A.GVKEY_N. Additional_Input.sas keeps only GVKEY, COPEROL, YEAR and DELTA in the downloaded RESULT.DELTA, so A.GVKEY_N is absent from that source. The already-created WORK.DELTA is the supported source for the join.

evidence.description: The datasheet names the historical vendor/source products for every included branch: I/B/E/S EPS, actuals, consensus, exclusions, stopped estimates, guidance; CRSP; Compustat; ExecuComp; Thomson Insiders; and Chapman IR data.
evidence.quote:
The raw data are obtained from various vendors that make their data available on Wharton
Research Data Services (WRDS) or from other sources as noted below. All data were downloaded
at various times between June 2016 and September 2020.

•   Individual forecasts data were downloaded in July 2016 from the I/B/E/S Unadjusted Detail—
    History file on WRDS.

•   Earnings announcement information were downloaded in July 2016 from the I/B/E/S
    Unadjusted Detail—Actuals on WRDS.

•   Analyst consensus data were downloaded in July 2016 from the I/B/E/S Unadjusted Summary
    History—Summary Statistics on WRDS.

•   Forecast removal information were downloaded in June 2017 from the I/B/E/S Unadjusted
    Detail—Excluded Estimates on WRDS.

•   Stopped estimates information were downloaded in June 2017 from the I/B/E/S Unadjusted
    Detail—Stopped Estimates on WRDS.

•   Management guidance data were downloaded in August 2017 from the I/B/E/S Guidance on
    WRDS.

•   Stock price data and stock split information were download in August 2017 from the CRSP
    Daily Stock file on WRDS.

•   Information on firm characteristics were downloaded in August 2017 from COMPUSTAT
    Fundamentals Quarterly on WRDS.

•   Investor relation officers data are from conference calls and were shared by Kimball Chapman

    in November 2017.

•   Information on S&P 500 index were downloaded in March 2018 from COMPUSTAT Index
    Constituents on WRDS.

•   Executive compensation data were downloaded in September 2020 from COMPUSTAT
    EXECUCOMP—Annual Compensation on WRDS.

•   Insider trading data were downloaded in September 2020 from Thomson Insiders Data on
    WRDS.

evidence.description: The datasheet states SAS sample construction, Stata winsorization and REGHDFE, and names the two supplied SAS programs.
evidence.quote:
We constructed the datasets for analyses using SAS. All continuous variables are winsorized in
STATA using WINSOR2. All the regression analyses are conducted in STATA using REGHDFE.
Section 3, Section 4, and Appendix B of the submitted manuscript describes the procedures of
sample construction and variable definitions. We also provide the following code to fulfill JAR’s
Data and Code Sharing Policy:

    •   “KMX_code.sas”: This SAS program produces the samples for our empirical analyses.

    •   “Additional_Input.sas”: This SAS program produces two additional datasets. One dataset
        serves as an additional input for the construction of the variable Optimism. The other is
        used for the construction of the variable Compensation Delta.

evidence.description: Additional_Input.sas describes two generated inputs and its initial RAW and RESULT library roots.
KMX_Code.sas names the EPS, GAAP, consensus, and cross-sectional products for Tables 2–6.
The optimism helper reads IBES_DETAIL_QTR and filters EPS estimates by forecast period and identifiers.
The optimism helper reads ACTUAL and builds quarterly EPS actuals.
The optimism helper reads DAILY_RET and uses NCUSIP, PERMNO, PRC, DATE and CFACSHR.

actions.description: Obtain or stage compatible underlying inputs for Additional_Input.sas: COMP.FUNDA, CRSP.CCMXPF_LNKHIST, CRSP.MSF, FRB.RATES_DAILY and each of six distinct ExecuComp tables. The authors’ remote WRDS session is one route; a documented compatible local source can substitute with coherent library-root configuration.
steps: Confirm authentication/component access for the SIGNON/RSUBMIT route, or document a compatible local staged-source route for the named tables; remote access is not assumed.

For either route, establish the annual Compustat 1986–2015 filter, dated CCM link rules, CRSP MSF 1–60 month lookback, six rate fields and 1992–2015 coverage, and 1992–2015 windows for all six ExecuComp sources.

For catalog candidates, verify live readability, required fields, period coverage, and any transformations/root changes before substituting them into the authored workflow. Exact author-file bytes/vintage are not required when a compatible route is documented.
validation: After the data route is authorized, compare actual source names, fields, fiscal/event date coverage and join keys against the cited code; catalog metadata alone does not establish a usable file.

actions.description: Obtain or construct compatible inputs for every distinct KMX RAW source used by the EPS, non-EPS/GPS, consensus, guidance, quarterly-accounting, index, monthly-CRSP, insider, annual-compensation, IR and earnings-volatility branches. Author-prepared filenames are a useful route where available; documented compatible local sources and constructions can also satisfy the contract.
steps: For each KMX RAW source, document a viable author-prepared or independently compatible source route with its fields, identifiers, complete dates, source product and construction; request author details only where those facts cannot otherwise be established.
Preserve the separate I/B/E/S DETAIL/ACTUAL/EXCLUDED/STOPPED EPS and non-EPS/GPS branches; do not substitute EPS-only records for the GPS branch.

Confirm Chapman IR records and each Compustat/CRSP/Thomson construction. Keep the IR contract, daily-return NCUSIP mapping, quarterly SIC mapping, and FRB DGS/TCMNOM mapping unresolved until documented.

For local catalog candidates, confirm the required code fields and complete coverage before staging them. CRSP MSP500LIST is not equivalent to Compustat SPIDX_CST; COMP.FUNDQ is not an author-prepared quarterly input until its SIC mapping, period and construction are established.
validation: Compare each delivered table’s product identity, source fields, units/identifiers, date ranges and linkage fields against its exact code consumer; keep unresolved cases undetermined.

actions.description: Resolve the required CRSP daily identifier contract before constructing RAW.DAILY_RET. The code joins actuals by CUSIP=NCUSIP and also needs split factors, prices, PERMNO and dates.
steps: Ask the authors to supply the prepared DAILY_RET file or document its NCUSIP creation/crosswalk and date-selection rule.
Do not infer NCUSIP from CRSP DSF CUSIP or silently rename the field.
validation: When the documented file/mapping is available, confirm the identifiers and field names used by the announcement-date and split-adjustment joins.

actions.description: Resolve the split local RESULT roots and hardcoded D: paths through one documented output-root configuration/staging step while retaining the remote WRDS session boundary.
steps: Set the local RAW and RESULT roots for the current machine and map every absolute Windows input/output in both entry programs to the agreed staged roots.
Make SE_190516 produced under RESULT available to KMX; stage or consistently rebind the downloaded delta from RESULT_202008 to the RESULT library KMX reads.
Preserve KMX’s native DTA export/import handoffs, including CROSS_EAVOL.DTA written before it is imported, and write all DTA outputs under one configured output root.
validation: Review the complete producer and consumer paths for SE_190516, DELTA, all result SAS tables and all DTA files before any authorized run.

steps: Check the installed SAS 9.4 runtime/version and the presence/configuration of SAS/CONNECT for SIGNON/RSUBMIT/PROC DOWNLOAD.
Check whether the SAS/ACCESS Interface to PC Files license/component supports the code’s DTA export and import DBMS identifiers.
Use Stata 18 for the exact embedded XTILE preparation snippets only after their input DTA files have been generated.
validation: Record successful version/component metadata and, after separate authorization, validate the specified handoff formats without running the author program during this assessment.

actions.description: Use the already-generated WORK.DELTA table, which contains the added GVKEY_N field, as the SQL source on line 1460.

The producer in Additional_Input.sas keeps only GVKEY, COPEROL, YEAR and DELTA in downloaded RESULT.DELTA, but this join refers to A.GVKEY_N. Using the generated WORK.DELTA supplies the exact already-authored key without changing formulas, samples or source records.

steps: Apply this exact one-line reference correction after confirming the frozen KMX_Code.sas hash and line content.
Retain the existing numeric GVKEY_N construction from the author code and preserve the original join keys and filters.

review_notes: Substantive full-pipeline draft saved from direct inspection of both supplied SAS programs, the datasheet, cached appendix text and frozen catalog metadata. All 88 frozen dependency IDs are classified below as source requirements or source-supported generated outputs/intermediates.
The only packaged data file is identifier.dta. Its cached probe reports only ibes_ticker; it is not a sample panel, a prepared input table or a substitute for the consumed RAW files.

The catalog is frozen resource metadata and saved product lookup output. It does not establish live access, file readability, complete historical coverage, author vintage or compatibility. No raw file was opened/read in this continuation.

All supplied main, GAAP/GPS, consensus, index, size, long/short, insider, compensation delta, IR, guidance, forecast-dispersion and earnings-volatility branches are retained. COMP_IBQ and CROSS_EAVOL are internal generated handoffs, not missing external inputs.

The datasheet describes WINSOR2 and REGHDFE in Stata, but the separate final regression scripts are not supplied. They remain contextual to this supplied data-preparation scope; no analysis-only route is claimed.

Stata metadata check confirmed `which _gxtile` at runtime version 18 only; no generated data, XTILE computation or syntax trial was performed. The uppercase command/function/option spelling in comments remains unresolved pending primary Stata help.

Source QA found a supported KMX delta join field-source mismatch: the author-created WORK.DELTA has GVKEY_N, while the downloaded RESULT.DELTA source does not. The proposal specifies a one-line FROM-source correction without changing the method or sample.

Compatible local source routes can satisfy raw inputs when their field, history, construction and staging contracts are independently documented; exact author-prepared file identity is not a mandatory gate.
